clinician.trajectory_summary: A 13-year-old boy presented with progressive vision loss, bilateral ptosis, restricted eye movements, and exotropia. Ophthalmologic examination revealed retinal hyperpigmentation and ellipsoid band disruption on OCT. Cardiac evaluation documented intermittent first-degree and partial second-degree AV block, consistent with KSS cardiac conduction defects. Brain MRI showed diffuse demyelinating lesions in cerebral white matter and brainstem regions. The patient had a history of growth retardation treated with growth hormone. Although genetic and muscle biopsy results confirming mitochondrial DNA deletions or mitochondrial pathology were not documented, the multisystemic clinical, ocular, cardiac, neurological, and historical findings support the diagnosis of KSS.
